subject: Post-demo: tool-calling + embeddings stack intermittent 5xx — next steps & repro
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@carlito.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: tool-calling + embeddings stack intermittent 5xx — next steps & repro

Hi Alex / Maria —

Thanks again for your time on the demo today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can move to a focused tech deep-dive:

What we saw
- You walked through the flow where requests include a structured tool call (function-like outputs) followed by an embeddings/reranker pass.
- Intermittent 5xx errors (502/504) show up in the middle of higher-concurrency batches — roughly 1–2% of production calls during burst test.
- You shared a short log snippet that contains request-id rb-11k9 and a 502 response; attached for reference.

What we need to repro
1) Minimal request payload (JSON) showing the structured output schema + reranker flags — please attach (you already referenced example-payload.json).
2) Exact SDK version + flags (beam/structuredOutput setting, model variant, batch config).
3) Any trace or request-id you observed around failures (we have rb-11k9).

Tentative hypothesis (from the demo)
- Routing / batching mismatch: a minority of requests with long kv-cache prefixes + structured-tool outputs may be routed to a fallback worker that isn't handling continuous-batching correctly, producing 5xx.

Immediate next steps (I propose):
- Alex: send the SDK snippet + full request payload for 2 failing requests (attachment or paste).
- Priyom: triage with an internal repro and come back with a short playbook (SAMPLING: lowering batch token thresholds, disabling prefix cache, increasing timeout).
- Connor / Ben: coordinate a 60-minute deep-dive Wed/Thu next week to run live repros and attach tracing.

I've attached: redwood-postcall-slide.pdf (slides from demo), example-payload.json (what you showed), short-log-snippet.txt (log you dropped in chat).

Propose we sync Tue/Wed — what's best for you?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: tool-calling + embeddings stack intermittent 5xx — next steps & repro

Stephanie — thanks for the recap. Quick notes and the reproduction details you asked for:

What we run in prod
- SDK: carlito-client-js v0.9.2 (we wrapped the Redwood SDK for our internal telemetry)
- Auth: API key in Authorization header (Bearer), keys scoped to org-account.
- Region: us-west (we hit your hosted endpoint).
- Model: rdx-large-1 (structured-output enabled). We also do a second call to an embeddings model for reranking (batch size 8).

Failure samples
- Request IDs where we saw 502/504: rb-11k9, rb-12a4, rb-12b0. Included short stack snippet below (sanitized):

---- start log ----
2026-11-21T22:43:12Z request_id=rb-11k9 status=502 worker=wn-17 stack=serve:batch:route:error
2026-11-21T22:43:12Z request_id=rb-11k9 payload_size=12kb seq_len=2048 cache_prefix_len=768
---- end log ----n

Repro steps we used (non-deterministic):
1) Send 16 concurrent requests with structured output + function call schema, followed immediately by an embeddings batch call (we do this in a client pipeline).
2) After 5–10 minutes of load, we see the 5xx spike.

I attached a sanitized example-payload.json — please let me know if you need the full raw request headers. We can also open a secure session for live repro if you prefer.

Can Priyom try the playbook you mentioned and share a quick canary recommendation? We're happy to accept a temporary config change if it stabilizes production.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Barnes
Head of Platform, Carlito AI
alex@carlito.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@carlito.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 12:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: tool-calling + embeddings stack intermittent 5xx — next steps & repro

Alex — thanks for the clear repro notes and the example payload. Quick triage / reproducibility plan from my side:

Initial observations
- The short log you shared (cache_prefix_len=768, seq_len=2048) points to long-prefix KV cache usage. If a worker that receives the request has a differing kernel path (quantized vs non-quantized) or if continuous-batching boundaries misalign, we can see transient 5xx when we try to materialize KV slices mid-batch.

Immediate repro steps for our lab (what I'll run)
1) Use your example-payload.json and the exact SDK headers (Authorization + X-Org-ID if you can provide).
2) Run a 16-concurrency burst with the same sequence lengths and a follow-on embeddings batch.
3) Capture raw trace headers (X-Request-ID, X-Redwood-Trace) and increase worker logs under route/batch.

Workarounds to test (targeted, low-risk)
- Temporary: set client.max_batch_tokens = 1024 (reduce from 4096) and client.max_concurrency = 8.
- Disable prefix caching for a short window: prefix_cache=false.
- Increase request timeout to 40s at client level.

Repro commands (curl example)
- We'll try to reproduce with a curl that mimics the SDK:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @example-payload.json -H 'X-Request-ID: repro-20261122-1'

I'll spin up the repro in our staging cluster and post results to SUP-7891. If we hit a 5xx, I'll include full worker logs and a stack trace.

I'll also add a short playbook to the drive: triage-playbook.md — contains the quick mitigation steps + exact config toggles.

One question for Alex / Carlito: do you have telemetry for how often a request has a large cache_prefix_len (>512)? That helps us reproduce more deterministically.

I'll follow up with a proposed Wed deep-dive slot after I have initial repro output.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Thanks Priyom — that plan looks good. A few quick answers:
- We see large prefix lengths about 18% of calls during heavy user sessions.
- We can provide X-Org-ID and a full header dump for two failing requests (I'll DM those to Priyom securely).

Can we try the temporary config changes (max_batch_tokens and prefix_cache=false) in a canary for one hour during our low-traffic window? Our ops team will run the changes if Redwood confirms it's safe for hosted endpoint. We're also curious about the latency impact — do you anticipate >10% tail latency on the reranker if we reduce batching?

We can join Wed 11/24 at 10:00 PT for the deep-dive (60m). Here's the meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/stephanie/carlito-deepdive — please confirm.

Appreciate it — Alex
